faqs.question: What time is Kali Puja in Kolkata on 28 October 2027?
faqs.answer: The nishita window in Kolkata runs from 10:55 PM to 11:45 PM IST on Thursday 28 October 2027, by our Astronomy Engine computation; Drik Panchang gives 10:55 to 11:46 PM. Amavasya has already been running for about two hours by then.

faqs.question: Why is Kali Puja on Thursday when Diwali is on Friday in 2027?
faqs.answer: Kali Puja needs Amavasya at midnight and Lakshmi Puja needs it just after sunset. Amavasya begins at about 8:48 PM on Thursday, too late for Thursday's pradosh but in time for its midnight, and ends at about 7:06 PM on Friday, which still covers Friday's pradosh but not Friday's midnight.

faqs.question: Was Kali Puja on the same day as Diwali in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. In 2026 Amavasya ran from 11:28 AM on Sunday 8 November to 12:32 PM on Monday 9 November, so Kali Puja and Lakshmi Puja both fell on Sunday night. 2027 is the year they separate by a day.

faqs.question: When does Amavasya begin and end for Kali Puja 2027?
faqs.answer: Amavasya begins at about 8:48 PM IST on Thursday 28 October 2027 and ends at about 7:06 PM on Friday 29 October. Drik Panchang lists 8:47 PM and 7:05 PM; our computation gives 8:49 PM and 7:07 PM, a difference that does not move either puja.

faqs.question: Is Bhoot Chaturdashi on 27 or 28 October 2027?
faqs.answer: On Thursday 28 October. Chaturdashi runs from 10:50 PM on Wednesday 27 October to 8:49 PM on Thursday, so Thursday's sunset falls inside it, and the fourteen lamps are lit on the same evening as Kali Puja, about four hours earlier.

faqs.question: What does Dipanwita mean?
faqs.answer: দীপান্বিতা (dīpānbitā) is the Bengali name for the Kartik new-moon night of Kali Puja. The Samsad Bengali-English dictionary defines it as the day when Goddess Kali is worshipped and houses are lit with rows of lamps; as an adjective it means lamped or illuminated.

faqs.question: Why is Kali also called Shyama?
faqs.answer: শ্যামা (śyāmā) is the feminine of শ্যাম, dark, and the Samsad dictionary lists Goddess Kali among its meanings. Thompson and Spencer's 1923 translation of Ramprasad's songs glosses Syama as the Dark Goddess, which is why the night is also called Shyama Puja.

faqs.question: Who was Ramprasad Sen, and why are his songs sung on Kali Puja night?
faqs.answer: Ramprasad Sen was an 18th-century Bengali poet whose songs to Kali make up most of Thompson and Spencer's 1923 selection of Shakta lyrics. Sister Nivedita wrote in 1900 that they survive as folk-songs full of the sentiment of Kali-worship, which is why Shyama sangeet fills the night.

faqs.question: Will offices in Kolkata close on 28 October 2027?
faqs.answer: Central government offices observe Diwali on Friday 29 October 2027 under the DoPT order, which lists Naraka Chaturdasi on 28 October only as a restricted holiday. West Bengal had not published its 2027 state list when we checked on 22 October 2026, so state offices are not yet confirmed.

faqs.question: When is Bhai Phonta in 2027?
faqs.answer: By our tithi computation, Sunday 31 October 2027, when Dwitiya holds at sunrise in Kolkata. Confirm the exact phonta time with a Bengali panjika, since family practice varies.

faqs.question: Should I send a Kali Puja greeting during the nishita puja?
faqs.answer: No. Between 10:55 and 11:45 PM in Kolkata the family is at the puja, and many keep a fast until it ends. Send before Thursday's 5:01 PM sunset or after the prasad, and keep the SubhSandesh Diwali page for Friday's Lakshmi Puja evening.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Kali Puja 2027: Thursday Night, a Day Before Lakshmi Puja

Kali Puja 2027 falls on Thursday 28 October 2027, one night before Diwali's Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October. Amavasya, the new-moon tithi, begins at about 8:48 PM IST on Thursday and ends at about 7:06 PM on Friday, so only Thursday has the new moon at midnight, and Kolkata's nishita window for the puja runs from 10:55 to 11:45 PM.

If you are greeting someone in Bengal from far away, the message will probably be read on a small screen: 48.3% of the 57,456 recorded views of shared SubhSandesh pages came from a phone. Our nearest festival data is Raksha Bandhan 2026, a different festival with only 89 pages, and 49.4% of those were built on the festival day itself. Below are nishita times for five cities, why Bhoot Chaturdashi shares the same evening, the night's sequence, and dictionary-checked Bengali words.

## What is Kali Puja, and why is 2027's on Thursday 28 October?

Kali Puja, also called Shyama Puja (শ্যামা পূজা, śyāmā pūjā), is the night worship of the goddess Kali on the Kartik new moon, kept mainly in West Bengal, Assam, Tripura and Odisha. Bengalis also call that night দীপান্বিতা (dīpānbitā), which the Samsad Bengali-English dictionary defines as ["the day of the new moon in the month of Kartik when Goddess Kali is worshipped"](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/cgi-bin/app/biswas-bengali_query.py?qs=%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%80%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE&searchhws=yes&matchtype=exact), with houses lit by rows of lamps.

The two pujas follow different clocks. Lakshmi Puja needs Amavasya during pradosh, the hours just after sunset, while Kali Puja needs Amavasya at nishita, the eighth of the fifteen equal parts of the night. In 2027 Amavasya starts too late on Thursday for pradosh but is well under way by midnight, and it ends at about 7:06 PM on Friday, long before Friday's midnight.

## Kali Puja 2027 in Kolkata, set against 2026

We computed these with the open-source [Astronomy Engine library](https://github.com/cosinekitty/astronomy), which its author describes as accurate to within ±1 arcminute and tested against NOVAS and JPL Horizons. Nishita is sunset plus seven to eight fifteenths of the night until sunrise, and Drik Panchang's pages for Kolkata, Guwahati, Bhubaneswar and New Delhi, used only as a date reference, agree to within one minute.

| Night | Date | What the rule needs | Kolkata window (IST) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bhoot Chaturdashi 2027 | Thu 28 Oct | Chaturdashi at dusk, until 8:49 PM | Lamps from 5:01 PM sunset |
| Kali Puja 2027 | Thu 28 Oct | Amavasya at midnight, from 8:49 PM | Nishita 10:55 to 11:45 PM |
| Lakshmi Puja 2027 | Fri 29 Oct | Amavasya in pradosh, until about 7:06 PM | 5:01 PM sunset to about 7:06 PM |
| Kali Puja 2026 | Sun 8 Nov | Amavasya at midnight | Nishita 10:54 to 11:46 PM |
| Lakshmi Puja 2026 | Sun 8 Nov | Amavasya in pradosh | From 4:55 PM sunset |

The takeaway is that 2027 stacks three observances into about 26 hours, where 2026 gave Kali and Lakshmi one shared Sunday. Elsewhere the 2027 nishita lasts about 50 minutes too, opening earlier the further east the sun sets:

- Guwahati: 10:41 to 11:32 PM
- Agartala: 10:43 to 11:34 PM
- Bhubaneswar: 11:05 to 11:55 PM
- New Delhi: 11:39 PM to 12:30 AM

## Bhoot Chaturdashi shares the same Thursday evening in 2027

Bhoot Chaturdashi (ভূত চতুর্দশী, bhūta caturdaśī) is the Chaturdashi evening before Kali Puja. The dictionary gives ভূত as a ghost or spirit and চতুর্দশী as the fourteenth day of a lunar fortnight, and many Bengali homes mark it with চৌদ্দ প্রদীপ (caudda pradīpa), fourteen lamps for the ancestors, and a dish of চৌদ্দ শাক (caudda śāka), fourteen leafy greens.

In 2027 Chaturdashi runs from 10:50 PM on Wednesday 27 October to 8:49 PM on Thursday 28 October by our computation. Thursday's sunset at 5:01 PM in Kolkata therefore falls inside Chaturdashi, so the fourteen lamps and the Kali Puja belong to one evening, about four hours apart.

In 2026 the two were separate evenings, Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November. If a household tradition keeps the greens for lunch, 2027 puts that lunch on Thursday too; check your own panjika before planning, since family practice varies.

## The night, hour by hour, on 28 October 2027

This is the general shape of a household or para (neighbourhood) Kali Puja in Bengal; families differ, and your own priest's vidhi comes first. Each step gives the Kolkata time, what happens and the Bengali word.

### 1. 5:01 PM: lamps at dusk

At Kolkata sunset the house is lit, starting with the fourteen Bhoot Chaturdashi lamps at doors and dark corners. The dictionary gives প্রদীপ (pradīpa) as a lamp and প্রদীপন as the lighting of lamps.

### 2. 8:48 PM: Amavasya begins

Around 8:48 PM IST the new-moon tithi starts and the night becomes দীপান্বিতা proper. Pandals finish dressing the image, the প্রতিমা (pratimā), usually a clay figure of Kali standing on Shiva. Red hibiscus, জবা (jabā), which the dictionary defines as a red species of China rose, is strung into garlands for the goddess.

### 3. 10:55 PM: the nishita puja

In Kolkata the main worship falls between 10:55 and 11:45 PM, the 50-minute nishita window. The priest offers flowers, lamps and food to the image while the family keeps the fast that many observe until the puja ends. Our honest advice is to send nothing during these 50 minutes; nobody in the room is looking at a phone.

### 4. After midnight: songs to Shyama

Late in the night many households and pandals sing Shyama sangeet, devotional songs to Kali, most famously by the 18th-century poet Ramprasad Sen. The prasad is shared, and the image stays until its বিসর্জন (bisarjana), the immersion, on a later day set by each puja committee.

## Ramprasad's songs and what two old books say about the night

Two public-domain books show how long this night has had its shape. Edward Thompson and Arthur Spencer's 1923 [Bengali Religious Lyrics, Śākta](https://archive.org/details/bengalireligious00thom), published in Calcutta and by Oxford University Press, notes that after Vijaya "on the next new moon night, the Kali-puja is held", with Durga tied to the bright half of the moon and Kali to the dark.

The same volume admits that "a scholarly edition of Ramprasad is badly wanted" and builds its selection mostly from his songs, glossing Syama as "the Dark Goddess". Sister Nivedita's 1900 essay collection [Kali the Mother](https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.215935) calls his output "a collection of folk-songs, full of the sentiment of Kali-worship, left to the memories of his people", many unrecorded in Bengal's villages.

Both were written by outsiders to Bengali devotion. We cite them for what they record, not as the last word.

## Is 28 October 2027 a holiday in Bengal?

Not yet confirmed for state offices. The Department of Personnel and Training's [2027 holiday order for central government offices](https://documents.doptcirculars.nic.in/D2/D02est/Holiday%20list%202027Cj0HU.PDF) lists Diwali on Friday 29 October 2027, and its paragraph 6 lets central offices move that holiday to Naraka Chaturdasi where a state declares only that day. Its restricted list already carries Naraka Chaturdasi on Thursday 28 October.

West Bengal's own 2027 list was not on the state's holiday page when we checked on 22 October 2026, which showed lists up to 2026. Until it appears, plan travel to Kolkata for Thursday 28 October as a possible working day.

## Bengali words for Kali Puja 2027, dictionary-checked

Every word below was checked in the Samsad dictionary on DSAL. শুভ (śubha), কালী (kālī) and পূজা (pūjā) are listed separately, though the joined কালীপূজা is not a headword.

- শুভ কালীপূজা (śubha kālīpūjā, "Shubho Kali Puja") — a blessed Kali Puja.
- অমাবস্যা (amābasyā) — the new moon.
- নিশীথ (niśītha) — midnight, late night; the root of "nishita".
- কার্তিক (kārtika) — the Bengali month, mid-October to mid-November.
- ভাইফোঁটা (bhāiphom̐ṭā) — Bhai Phonta, the brother's forehead mark, which our computation puts on Sunday 31 October 2027, when Dwitiya holds at sunrise.

Three original lines follow, in English with one Bengali phrase. Each names a detail of this year's night:

- "Shubho Kali Puja. May the fourteen lamps tonight light every corner, and the fifteenth one be you."
- "Thursday night, 10:55 in Kolkata. I will be thinking of the pandal and the jaba garlands from here."
- "A blessed Shyama Puja to the whole para, from someone who will be humming Ramprasad at midnight."

## Sending a Kali Puja greeting from away

SubhSandesh has no Kali Puja template, and we would rather say so than stretch one. The closest is the [interactive Diwali card on SubhSandesh](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali): they light a diya at their door with your tag, a row of wish diyas, a rangoli that glows with your initials, and sky lanterns holding up to six photos. A letter opens from a red-and-gold liffafa, and the drawn crackers make no noise or smoke.

It takes about five minutes, opens from a private link in any browser with no app or account, and has love, family and friend modes. It says Shubh Deepavali, not Kali, so it suits Friday's Lakshmi Puja evening better than Thursday's puja. Shared SubhSandesh pages average 11.1 views each, so a page sent on Friday can be reopened over the weekend.

For a partner who could not get home to Kolkata this year, the [miss-you page with a countdown to your next visit](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits better, because it is built for someone far away. Of 214 miss-you pages made since July 2026, 43.5% were password-protected; that is two months of data and says nothing about festivals.

## When a link is the wrong way to mark Kali Puja 2027

For a grandparent fasting until the puja ends after 11:45 PM, a phone call before 5 PM or after the prasad does more than any page. If you are in the same city, walking to the para pandal with them is the gift.

The Raksha Bandhan figures above also cut against planning early: 27.0% of those 89 pages were built the day before, and none more than 7 days ahead. For Kali Puja that suggests Wednesday 27 October is soon enough to prepare a message, and the greeting itself can wait until the puja is over.

The only table sets Kolkata's 2027 nights (Bhoot Chaturdashi, Kali Puja, Lakshmi Puja) against 2026's, with the tithi rule and the IST window; it was redesigned so it does not repeat kojagari-lakshmi-puja-2027's city-by-nishita table. SubhSandesh has no Kali Puja or Bengal-specific usage data, and /happy-diwali is new, so no first-party column could be added without inventing one. Closes if a Diwali/Kali Puja 2027 segment is ever measured (re-query after 29 Oct 2027).

failed.item: No source passes the **swap test** — none could sit unchanged in a different keyword's post in this batch
failed.why: Two of six sources would fit another 2027 date post in this batch: the DoPT 2027 holiday order (already cited by chhath-puja-2027) and the Astronomy Engine library used for the timings. They carry the Naraka Chaturdasi clause and the nishita computation, which are load-bearing here, so they stay; the other four (Thompson and Spencer 1923, Nivedita 1900, the Samsad dictionary entries, the Kolkata/Guwahati/Bhubaneswar Drik date reference) are specific to Kali Puja.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the five pages analysed: it is the only one giving Kolkata, Guwahati, Agartala and Bhubaneswar nishita windows with a stated method, it catches that calendarena prints the wrong 2027 date and that Bhoot Chaturdashi shares the Thursday evening, and its Bengali terms are dictionary-checked. It cannot overcome Drik Panchang's authority on a date query or SubhSandesh having no Kali Puja template and no Bengal usage data; the timing table carries no first-party column.

structuralLimitations: SERP measured on DuckDuckGo HTML (kl=in-en), lower confidence than Google India: WebSearch hit its session cap and Firecrawl credits ran out. Top 5 fetched with node fetch (ctx sandbox); panchangya returned 403.

USNO (aa.usno.navy.mil) refused connections from the sandbox on 22 Oct 2026 (fetch failed), so no USNO URL is cited. All astronomical times were computed with Astronomy Engine 2.1.19 (VSOP87/NOVAS-based, ±1 arcminute) rather than the NOAA sunrise equation; nishita = sunset + 7/15 to 8/15 of the sunset-to-sunrise night. Results matched Drik Panchang to within one minute for Kolkata, Guwahati, Bhubaneswar and New Delhi; Agartala was computed only.

Drik Panchang ranks #5 for this keyword. Per BRIEF §1 it is used only as a date/festival reference in batchMeta.sources (marked), not linked in the body; the body names it as the comparison for our computed times.

Amavasya start differs by 2 minutes between Drik Panchang (8:47 PM) and our computation (8:49 PM); the body uses 'about 8:48 PM' and states both. Amavasya end: Drik 7:05 PM, ours 7:07 PM, BRIEF's USNO figure 7:06 PM; body says 'about 7:06 PM'.
BRIEF/b1 claim 'Kali Puja 28 Oct 2027' verified as correct. calendarena.com (SERP #2) prints Friday 29 October 2027, which contradicts the nishita rule.

Bhoot Chaturdashi customs (fourteen lamps, fourteen greens) are stated as widespread household practice; no fetched source documents them. The dictionary confirms the words (ভূত, চতুর্দশী, চৌদ্দ, প্রদীপ, শাক) but not the custom, and ভূতচতুর্দশী is not a Samsad headword. Its 2027 date (28 Oct) and 2026 date (7 Nov) are from our tithi computation.
Bhai Phonta 31 Oct 2027 is from our tithi computation (Dwitiya at Kolkata sunrise) and agrees with BRIEF's Bhai Dooj date; the body tells readers to confirm with a panjika.

No peer-reviewed open-access paper on Kali Puja ritual was found. findpapers.mjs queries tried: 'Kali Puja Bengal', 'Kali Puja Diwali Kolkata fireworks air', 'Shyama Kali goddess worship Bengal ritual', 'Kali Puja Assam Kamakhya', 'Kali Puja Diwali festival Kolkata noise'; Europe PMC full-text '"Kali Puja"' returned only air-quality and cannabis papers that mention it in passing, and the Oxford University Press monographs Crossref surfaced ('Singing to the Goddess', 2001; 'Mother of My Heart, Daughter of My Dreams', 2001) are paywalled. The scholarly requirement is met by Thompson and Spencer 1923 (OUP, public domain) as a public-domain primary/scholarly text, which BRIEF §5 permits for ritual posts.
West Bengal's 2027 holiday list was not on par.wb.gov.in/holidaylist.php on 22 Oct 2026 (lists up to 2026); not linked because it evidences an absence. The 2026 PDF link on that page returned 404.
The joined greeting কালীপূজা is not a Samsad headword; its parts কালী and পূজা are, and the body says so.
